Here's a summary of what the search turned up. The sources are mostly third-party guides, not official Anthropic documentation, so treat the specifics as community advice.

- **Core structure:** A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file that holds YAML frontmatter and markdown instructions. One source calls the description field the trigger and suggests spending most of your writing effort there (https://codemeetai.substack.com/p/how-to-create-a-claude-code-skill).
- **Progressive loading:** One guide says only each skill's name and description load at session start, and the full SKILL.md is read only when relevant (https://runtm-dep-5f39a156.runtm.com/best-practices/skills/).
- **Descriptions:** Guides recommend a specific description with trigger phrases, and one suggests gerund-style names like "writing-release-notes" (https://runtm-dep-5f39a156.runtm.com/best-practices/skills/). Another suggests phrasing descriptions as "Use when..." triggering conditions (https://www.skills.sh/v1-io/v1tamins/skilling-it).
- **Testing:** One approach is to ask Claude to do the task without the slash command and check whether the skill loads. If it doesn't, the description is probably too vague (https://runtm-dep-5f39a156.runtm.com/best-practices/skills/).
- **Scope:** A skill-writing guide advises first checking whether Claude actually needs the skill by testing its baseline without one (https://www.skills.sh/meriley/claude-code-skills/skill-writing). Another says project-specific conventions belong in CLAUDE.md instead (https://openskillindex.com/skills/diegosouzapw-awesome-omni-skill-writing-skills-0bec00).
- **Locations:** Personal skills go in ~/.claude/skills/, project skills in .claude/skills/ (committable to the repo), and when names collide, enterprise beats personal, which beats project (https://sherlock.xyz/post/how-to-write-skills-for-claude-code-and-cowork).
- **Supporting files:** Scripts, templates, and reference docs can sit beside SKILL.md and be referenced from it (https://sherlock.xyz/post/how-to-write-skills-for-claude-code-and-cowork).
- **Examples from Anthropic:** An Anthropic blog post on how the team uses skills lists categories like testing practices, CI/CD and deployment, and runbooks for debugging (https://claude.com/blog/lessons-from-building-claude-code-how-we-use-skills).

For authoritative guidance, the Anthropic docs on skills should be checked directly, since I didn't find them in these results.

content.text:
Here are the best practices from my search. Most sources are third-party guides, not official Anthropic documentation, so treat the details as community advice.

**Structure**
- A skill is a folder with a `SKILL.md` file. The file has YAML frontmatter (name, description) followed by markdown instructions.
- Loading is progressive. Only each skill's name and description load at session start, and the full body loads when Claude judges it relevant. Keep the body focused, and put scripts, templates and reference docs in supporting files that `SKILL.md` points to. ([runtm guide](https://runtm-dep-5f39a156.runtm.com/best-practices/skills/), [Sherlock](https://sherlock.xyz/post/how-to-write-skills-for-claude-code-and-cowork))

**Description**
- The description is what triggers the skill, so spend most of your writing effort on it. Make it specific and include the phrases a user would actually say. ([CodeMeetAI](https://codemeetai.substack.com/p/how-to-create-a-claude-code-skill))
- Phrase it as a triggering condition, for example "Use when…". ([skilling-it](https://www.skills.sh/v1-io/v1tamins/skilling-it))
- Use clear names. One guide suggests gerund style, such as `writing-release-notes`. ([runtm guide](https://runtm-dep-5f39a156.runtm.com/best-practices/skills/))

**Scope**
- Before writing a skill, test whether Claude already does the task well without one. ([skill-writing](https://www.skills.sh/meriley/claude-code-skills/skill-writing))
- Put project-wide conventions in `CLAUDE.md` rather than in a skill. ([writing-skills](https://openskillindex.com/skills/diegosouzapw-awesome-omni-skill-writing-skills-0bec00))
- Anthropic's own skills cover narrow areas such as testing practices, CI/CD and deployment, and debugging runbooks. ([Anthropic blog](https://claude.com/blog/lessons-from-building-claude-code-how-we-use-skills))

**Testing**
- Ask Claude to do the task without invoking the slash command. If the skill doesn't load, the description is probably too vague. ([runtm guide](https://runtm-dep-5f39a156.runtm.com/best-practices/skills/))

**Location**
- Personal skills go in `~/.claude/skills/`. Project skills go in `.claude/skills/`, which you can commit to the repo.
- If names collide, enterprise skills override personal ones, and personal ones override project ones. ([Sherlock](https://sherlock.xyz/post/how-to-write-skills-for-claude-code-and-cowork))

My search didn't surface Anthropic's official skill-authoring docs. If you want, I can fetch those next to check the points above against them.

Sources:
- [How to create a Claude Code skill](https://codemeetai.substack.com/p/how-to-create-a-claude-code-skill)
- [Lessons from building Claude Code: How we use skills](https://claude.com/blog/lessons-from-building-claude-code-how-we-use-skills)
- [How to Write Skills for Claude Code and Cowork](https://sherlock.xyz/post/how-to-write-skills-for-claude-code-and-cowork)
- [skill writing](https://www.skills.sh/meriley/claude-code-skills/skill-writing)
- [writing-skills](https://openskillindex.com/skills/diegosouzapw-awesome-omni-skill-writing-skills-0bec00)
- [Best practice (runtm)](https://runtm-dep-5f39a156.runtm.com/best-practices/skills/)
- [skilling it](https://www.skills.sh/v1-io/v1tamins/skilling-it)
